# agentbus client API

> agentbus runs on your machine, between coding agents (Claude Code, codex) and their vendors.
> It records each step of their work as an event, in one local store.
> This API lets any program read those events, start agents, and write its own events.

This file is a short guide. The full reference is generated from the code when the service starts:
the OpenAPI 3.1 description at `GET /api/v0/openapi.json`, and an interactive page built from it at
`/docs`. Both are served by the service itself, without the token and without internet. There are no
client SDKs: call the endpoints directly, or generate a client from the description. The contract in
words is `docs/CLIENT_API.md` in the repository.

## Modes

`agentbus up` runs everything in one process: the API, the job queue, the record, the gateway and a
runner. `agentbus server` is the same with no runner. `agentbus runner -server <url>` takes jobs
from a server and runs them on its machine, with its own record and gateway; its own API has no
job routes. This file describes the API of `up` and `server`.

## Address and token

- The service listens on `http://127.0.0.1:8787` by default. `agentbus up -listen 0.0.0.0`
  makes it reachable from the network, such as from outside a container. With no port, 8787.
- Every request except `/api/v0/openapi.json` and `/docs` sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- `GET /` redirects to `/docs`.
- The token is the file `token` in the data folder: `$AGENTBUS_HOME`, else
  `$XDG_DATA_HOME/agentbus`, else `~/.local/share/agentbus`.
- `permissions.toml` in the data folder has three lists: `read_folders`, `allow` and `forbid`, the
  `edit` rule, the `subagents` switch, `[limits]` and `[agent_api]`. A key left out reads as its
  default. Every turn reads it when it starts; the API reads it for each request a turn token
  sends. claude gets one
  `--allowedTools` with `Read(//<folder>/**),Grep(//<folder>/**),Glob(//<folder>/**)` per folder
  (reading only) and `Bash(<cmd>:*)` per allowed command, and `--disallowedTools Bash(<cmd>:*),…`. A
  `read_only` turn ignores `allow`. `forbid` applies to claude and codex through the gateway: a
  shell command in a model reply that matches an entry is refused before the agent can run it, and a
  `tool.refused` event is stored. The command is parsed as shell and each simple command in it is
  matched alone, and git's global options are skipped, so `git -C repo push` matches `git push`. It
  reads text only: a command built at run time or run from a script is not seen, so a hard rule
  also needs the agent to lack what the command needs (no push credentials). codex gets nothing from
  `read_folders` and `allow`. `edit = "session"` (default) lets a turn edit its own session folder
  without asking: claude gets `Edit(//<folder>/**)`, codex `--sandbox workspace-write` with network;
  `edit = "none"` gives claude `--disallowedTools Edit,Write,NotebookEdit`, which wins over the
  person's own settings, and codex `--sandbox read-only`. `subagents = false` (default true) stops
  a turn starting the agent's own subagents: claude gets `--disallowedTools Task,Agent,Workflow`,
  codex `--disable multi_agent --disable multi_agent_v2`; no settings file is edited. No turn edits the data
  folder's own files (`permissions.toml`, `instructions.md`, `agents.json`, the tokens): claude gets
  a deny rule on each. `[limits]`: `max_depth` (2), `max_jobs_per_turn` (10), `max_jobs_per_tree`
  (30), `max_cost_usd_per_tree` (0, off). `[agent_api]`: `scope` (`"tree"` or `"session"`), and
  `read`, `list_agents`, `start`, `continue`, `review`, `cancel`, `rename`, `apply`, each true unless set false. A
  broken file answers 400 and nothing is stored; a turn token's requests get 503 then. A missing
  file is every default.
- `instructions.md` in the data folder is the text every turn gets as its agent's own instruction
  (`--append-system-prompt`, `developer_instructions`), with `{session}` replaced by the session id.
  Missing: the default text. Empty: none.
- Settings through the API, main token only: `GET`/`PUT /api/v0/settings/permissions` (the policy
  as JSON) and `GET`/`PUT /api/v0/settings/instructions` (`{"text": "..."}`). A `PUT` sends
  `If-Match` with the `ETag` of a `GET`, or `*`; a stale one gets 412, none 428. A turn token gets
  403 on all four: an agent never reads or changes its own policy. A runner started with
  `agentbus runner -server <url>` reads the server's policy and instructions before each turn; when
  the server cannot be reached the turn does not start and the job fails with that reason.
- The turns token, the file `turns_token` in the data folder (`abq_` and 64 hex characters), may
  only start, stop and read turns: `POST /api/v0/turns`, `GET /api/v0/turns`,
  `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}`, `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/events` and `POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/stop`.
  Every other route gets 403. A job queue or a runner uses it in place of the main token. To
  replace it, stop the service, delete the file and start again.
- Never put the token in a URL. In a browser, read the stream with `fetch`, not `EventSource`.
- A browser page from any origin may call the API: CORS answers `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`
  and allows the `Authorization` header. No cookies are used; the token is the guard.
  `agentbus up -origin <url>` locks it to one origin.
- On loopback, the `Host` header must be `127.0.0.1:<port>`, `localhost:<port>` or `[::1]:<port>`,
  or the answer is 403. On another address any `Host` is accepted; the token is the guard.
- Every error is JSON: `{"error": "..."}`, with fixed wording.

```sh
TOKEN=$(cat "${AGENTBUS_HOME:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/agentbus}/token")
B=http://127.0.0.1:8787
```

## Inside a turn: `$AGENTBUS_URL` and `$AGENTBUS_TOKEN`

If you are an agent that agentbus started (`POST /api/v0/turns`), your environment has:

- `AGENTBUS_URL`: the service's address, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8787`.
- `AGENTBUS_TOKEN`: a token for your turn only. It stops working when your turn ends. Never print
  it, log it or write it to a file; use the variable's name.

It reads your **request tree**: your own session, the person's session you were started from, and
every session work in that tree started. That covers `GET /api/v0/turns` (`session` defaults to
yours), `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}`, `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/events`, `GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/events`,
`GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/search`, `GET /api/v0/calls/{id}/context` and `/pieces/{n}`,
`GET /api/v0/jobs?session=…`, `GET /api/v0/jobs/{id}`, and `GET /api/v0/agents` and
`GET /api/v0/harnesses`. Your session id is the `<session>` in your base URL
(`.../s/<session>/t/<turn>`, in `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` for claude), and every turn
`GET /api/v0/turns` lists carries it. Every turn is also told this in its instructions (claude:
`--append-system-prompt`; codex: `developer_instructions`), with its session id filled in: four
lines, the same on every turn of the session, never added to the prompt. A codex turn gets none
when the person set `developer_instructions` in codex's own config, so theirs is kept.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTBUS_TOKEN" "$AGENTBUS_URL/api/v0/turns"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTBUS_TOKEN" "$AGENTBUS_URL/api/v0/sessions/abc/search?q=login"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTBUS_TOKEN" "$AGENTBUS_URL/api/v0/calls/x-9f2c01ab-7/pieces/12"
```

## Ask other agents

With the same token you can hand work to other agents. Do not wait for it: start it, say so, and
end your turn. **Each result comes back to your session as a later turn**, whose prompt starts
`[AgentBus] This message is from AgentBus, not from the person`. It names the agent, its session
and folder, the changed files, a review's verdict, and the agent's final reply.

1. List the agents: `GET /api/v0/agents`. Use an agent's `id`.
2. Start a turn on one: `POST /api/v0/turns` with `agent` and `prompt`. Leave `folder` out: the
   new session works on its own copy of the person's folder, so several agents can work on the
   same task without touching each other's files or the person's. To fan out ("run all 3 on this"),
   start one turn per agent; each result comes back on its own.
3. Continue a session you started: `POST /api/v0/turns` with that `session` and `prompt`.
4. Ask for a review of a turn's work once its job has ended: `POST /api/v0/jobs/{job}/review` with
   `agent` (the job id is in the reply of step 2, as `job`).
5. Cancel work you asked for: `POST /api/v0/jobs/{job}/cancel`.
6. See what a turn did: `GET /api/v0/turns/{turn}/diff`. Put its changes in the person's folder:
   `POST /api/v0/turns/{turn}/apply`. A 409 lists each file that changed there since the turn
   started, with why, and nothing is written: read it, then make another turn that resolves it.

Use `agentbus-api METHOD PATH [BODY]`, which is on your PATH. It sends your token for you, so the
command holds no variable and needs no approval. curl with the header works too, where your tools
allow it.

```sh
agentbus-api GET /api/v0/agents
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/turns '{"agent":"codex","prompt":"Add a test for parse() in parse_test.go"}'
# {"id":"<session>","turn":"t_…","job":"job_…","base_url":"…"}
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/jobs/job_…/review '{"agent":"claude"}'
```

Refused with 403, with the reason: a read-only turn asking for anything; a `folder` outside your
own; `isolate: false`; continuing your own session or the person's; changing agents or policy;
anything about tokens; making a job with `POST /api/v0/jobs`; any session outside your tree; a call
the person switched off in `[agent_api]` of `permissions.toml` (the refusal names the switch).
Limits, `[limits]` there, by default: work goes at most 2 levels below the person's turn
(`max_depth`), one turn asks for at most 10 jobs (`max_jobs_per_turn`), one person's session for at
most 30 in all (`max_jobs_per_tree`), and no cost cap (`max_cost_usd_per_tree`). The refusal names
the limit reached.

## Starting up: snapshot, then stream

1. `GET /api/v0/sessions` returns every session and the `store` and `seq` it was computed at.
2. `GET /api/v0/events?store=<store>&after=<seq>` streams every event after that point, then new ones.

An event that lands between the two calls is in the stream, not in the snapshot. Nothing is lost or
counted twice. To resume after a disconnect, reconnect with the last `store` and `seq` you saw.

The cursor is the pair `store` and `seq`. If the `store` you send is not the current one, the answer
is 409 with the current `store` in the body: start over from step 1.

## Endpoints

### GET /api/v0/sessions

The sessions, newest activity first, with tokens, cost, open state and title (the latest rename,
else the first message). `agent` and `folder`
come from the session's latest turn that names them. `open` is true while a turn's agent for the
session is running. A session groups turns; `GET /api/v0/turns` lists the turns themselves.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $B/api/v0/sessions
# {"store":"st_9f2c…","seq":1041,"sessions":[{"id":"abc","agent":"claude","open":true,"turns":7,…}]}
```

### PATCH /api/v0/sessions/{id}

Rename a session: body `{"title":"..."}`, 1 to 120 characters on one line. It stores a
`session.renamed` event with `title` and `old_title`; the list then shows the latest name, and
earlier names stay in the session's events. A rename does not change `last`. A turn token may
rename a session in its scope unless `rename = false` in `[agent_api]`; a read-only turn may not.

```sh
curl -s -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"Login fix"}' $B/api/v0/sessions/abc
# {"seq":1042,"id":"evt_…","title":"Login fix","old_title":"Fix the login bug"}
```

### GET /api/v0/events

A live stream (`text/event-stream`). Each message is `id: <store>/<seq>`, `event: <kind>`,
`data: <one event as JSON>`, then a blank line. `: ping` comes every 15 seconds. `session=<id>`
limits it to one session. Without `store` and `after` it starts with new events only.

```sh
curl -sN -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/events?store=st_9f2c…&after=1041"
```

### GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/events

One session's stored events, oldest first, a page at a time. `limit` is 1 to 10000 (default 1000).
`next_after` is the `after` for the next page, or null.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/sessions/abc/events?store=st_9f2c…&after=0&limit=100"
```

### POST /api/v0/turns

Start a turn. Every turn runs as a job: this makes a turn job and answers once a runner has started
its turn (the reply also names the `job`). Without `session`: a saved agent (its id from `GET /api/v0/agents`; a new data folder has `claude` and `codex`) with a prompt in a folder, in a new
session. The agent's harness, access and model start it; `model` sent here wins. A new session works on its own copy of its folder, as the `isolation` setting of `permissions.toml` says (`auto`, the default: an APFS clone on macOS, an overlay mount on Linux where the runner can mount one, else a copy; `overlay`; `copy`; `git`, a git worktree in a repo; `none`; `share_read_only` lists top-level folders such as `node_modules` that a copy links read-only instead of copying, and a turn cannot write there), starting from the folder exactly as it is; nothing reaches the folder until a turn is applied (`POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/apply`). Send `"isolate": false` to use the folder as it is. With `session`: the next turn of a session the snapshot marks `resumable`, in its own folder
(send none, or the session's own; a different one is refused with 400). It runs on the session's
latest agent, or on the saved agent `agent` names: any message may go to any agent, and later
turns stay on it. A switch takes the agent's model; naming the session's own latest agent keeps
the session's model, decided when the turn starts. On the same harness the conversation continues by own replay; on another harness
(or codex on OpenRouter) the agent gets the earlier turns as plain text before the person's words,
and its `turn.started` has `continuity: "transcript"` with that text in `context`. Answers 202
as soon as it starts, with the session `id` and the new `turn` id. Every event of the turn carries
that id in `turn`, and its `turn.started` (with the prompt) is stored before the reply. `read_only`
is false unless true. True gives claude Read, Grep and Glob only, and codex `--sandbox read-only`.
False leaves claude its own tools and settings plus the `edit` rule of `permissions.toml` (by default
`Edit(//<folder>/**)`), and, with `edit = "session"`, gives codex `--sandbox workspace-write` with
network on (`-c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true`): it can edit the folder and reach the
network, so it can call this API with its turn token. Read-only codex has no writes and no network. 404 for an unknown session, 409 when the session
cannot be continued. A turn sent while the session's turn runs, or while others wait, is queued
behind them and runs next, in order: 202 at once with `"queued":true`, its `job`, and `ahead`, how
many of the session's turns are before it. At most 4 turns running at once, or the number `agentbus up -max-runs <n>` sets;
a turn no runner starts within 30 seconds answers 202 with `"queued":true`, its `job` and session `id`, and no `turn`: it runs later.
`idempotency_key` (optional, 1 to 128 of `A-Za-z0-9._:-`) makes a retry safe: the same key with
the same fields answers 202 with the same turn and `"existing":true`, and starts nothing; the same
key with other fields gets 409. The key is the turn job's key; a request refused with 400 before it is queued uses none. There is no `/api/v0/runs`. An agent
whose program is not on the service's PATH gets 400 and nothing is stored: `agent claude cannot
start: the program claude is not on the service's PATH. Install Claude Code and run claude once to
sign in, then try again. If it is installed, start agentbus from a shell where claude runs.`
`GET /api/v0/harnesses` shows which harnesses the service finds.

claude and codex both continue by own replay: the agent starts fresh, with no `--resume` or
`exec resume`, its `turn.started` names the earlier turn in `replay_from`, and the gateway puts
that turn's whole history in front of each of the turn's model requests. For claude that is
messages, tool calls, tool results and thinking blocks as sent and received. For codex it is input
items and the reply's output items, encrypted reasoning byte for byte, and the gateway also writes
the session's first thread id over the fresh one (body and headers) so the history is read from
cache. If it cannot, it stores `replay.failed` and the turn fails, rather than run without its
past. `replay_from` is always the newest turn. If that turn did not finish (its agent was stopped,
the service restarted mid-turn, or its last model call failed), the next turn still continues: the
history is what that turn did, with an error result for each tool call that got no result
(`tool_result`, or codex's `function_call_output` / `custom_tool_call_output`), then a note
starting `[Note from AgentBus, not written by the model]` (an assistant message for claude, a
developer message for codex) saying how it ended and to check the folder. A turn that never
reached the model adds the person's message and a note that it was not acted on. The next turn's
`turn.started` then carries `recovered_from` and `recovered_reason`. The 409 for a session that
cannot be continued gives the reason, naming the turn (such as one that may be missing events, or
whose last request was compacted). `agentbus up -replay=false` puts both on the vendor's resume (a
session already continued by replay is then refused with 409), and a session from before replies
were kept continues by the vendor's resume. A next turn's `turn.started` says which it used in
`continuity` (`replay`, `resume` or `transcript`).

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"agent":"codex","folder":"/Users/ana/Sites/x","prompt":"Review the last commit"}' $B/api/v0/turns
# {"id":"abc","turn":"t_5d0c…","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8787/s/abc/t/t_5d0c…"}
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"session":"abc","prompt":"Now fix the second one"}' $B/api/v0/turns
# {"id":"abc","turn":"t_91ee…","base_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8787/s/abc/t/t_91ee…"}
```

### GET /api/v0/turns

The turns, newest first, with `store` and `seq` like the sessions snapshot, so you can stream from
there. Each has `id`, `session`, `agent`, `folder`, `prompt`, `started`, `ended` (when done),
`state` (`running`, `finished`, `failed`), `outcome`, `exit_code`, `stopped` (true when the
person stopped it), `usage`, `cost_usd` and `cost_complete`. A started turn's `state` comes from its agent's exit: 0 is `finished`, anything else
`failed`. `prompt` is the first 500 characters, with `prompt_truncated: true` when cut; the whole
prompt is the `text` of the turn's `turn.started` in `/turns/{id}/events`. `reply` is the first 500
characters of the reply to the turn's last model call, with `reply_truncated: true` when cut; it is
empty while that reply has not come. `model` is the model that last call asked for, and
`model_calls` counts the turn's `model.requested` events. `session=<id>` filters
to one session. `limit` is 1 to 1000 (default 100), and a page also stops at 4 MiB of rows; for
older turns send `before=<next_before>` until it is null.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/turns?session=abc"
# {"store":"st_9f2c…","seq":1041,"turns":[{"id":"t_91ee…","session":"abc","state":"running",…}],"next_before":null}
```

### GET /api/v0/turns/{id}

One turn, with the same fields as a row of `GET /api/v0/turns`, plus `store` and `seq`. Poll it to
wait for a turn to end: `state` leaves `running`. Every turn row also has `unsettled` (true when the
gateway could not confirm every model call was stored, as after a restart), `error` (why the agent
could not start) and `idempotency_key` (when it was started with one). `session=<id>` picks one
session's turn; without it the newest. 404 when no `turn.started` carries the id.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/turns/t_91ee…"
# {"store":"st_9f2c…","seq":1052,"turn":{"id":"t_91ee…","session":"abc","state":"finished","exit_code":0,…}}
```

### POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/stop

Stop a running turn: this cancels its job, and the runner stops the turn within 2 seconds. Its agent and every process it started end, as when the service stops:
SIGTERM to the whole tree, then SIGKILL after 5 seconds to what still runs. The reply is 202
`{"id":"<session>","turn":"<turn>"}` at once; the turn's `session.closed`, with `stopped: true`,
comes once the tree has ended, and `GET /api/v0/turns` then shows `stopped: true`. The session's
next turn continues after it, and the model is told the person stopped it (`recovered_reason`
ends with `the person stopped this turn`). A second stop while it is stopping gets 202 again and
sends nothing more. 409 when the turn is not running (its job ended, or it is not a job of this service),
404 when no job or event carries the turn id. The main token or the turns token; a turn token only for a turn its tree asked for. No body.

```sh
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/turns/t_91ee…/stop"
# {"id":"abc","turn":"t_91ee…"}
```

### GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/diff

Everything the record holds about what one turn did, in one answer. `files`: each file it added,
modified or deleted, with size and SHA-256, and in an isolated copy each small text file's own
unified diff (`diff`); `diff_left_out` marks a file whose content changed and has no diff here
(binary, over 256 KiB, past the 512 KiB budget, or its earlier content no longer kept). `files` is
null while the turn runs. `model_calls`: count, usage, cost, calls per model, and each call with
its `exchange`. `tools`: each tool call with its input (up to 4 KiB), error and any refusal.
`commands`: the shell commands it asked to run, as the gateway reads them. Also the agent,
started, ended, `duration_ms`, and `apply`: whether its changes were applied (`state` none, queued,
running, applied, refused or failed). A turn token reads it for a turn in its scope.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $B/api/v0/turns/t_9f2c01ab4d5e6f70/diff
# {"turn":"t_…","files":{"isolated":true,"from":"base","to":"t_…","count":1,"changes":[{"path":"a.txt","change":"modified","diff":"--- a/a.txt\n+++ b/a.txt\n@@ …"}]},"model_calls":{"count":3,…},"commands":["go test ./..."],"apply":{"state":"none"}}
```

### POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/apply

Put one turn's file changes into the person's folder: the folder its session's copy was made from.
No body. 200 with `state: "applied"` and `files` written. If any file there is neither as it was at
the turn's start nor already as the turn left it, nothing is written: 409 with `state: "refused"`,
`error`, and `conflicts` (`path` and `why` for each). Applying the same turn again is a no-op: 200
with `already: true`. A refused apply may be asked for again. 202 when the runner has not finished
within 30 seconds; the turn's diff shows how it ended. 400 for a turn that cannot be applied (still
running, or not in an isolated copy, or its session closed). A turn token may apply a turn in its
scope unless `apply = false` in `[agent_api]`; a read-only turn may not.

```sh
curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $B/api/v0/turns/t_9f2c01ab4d5e6f70/apply
# {"state":"applied","turn":"t_…","session":"abc","job":"job_…","files":["a.txt"],"pruned":true}
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/turns/t_9f2c01ab4d5e6f70/apply
# 409 {"state":"refused","conflicts":[{"path":"a.txt","why":"changed in your folder since the checkpoint"}],…}
```

### GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/events

One turn's stored events, oldest first, paged like a session's events. `events.dropped` names
sessions, not turns, so it is not among them. The same turn id can be in two sessions: send
`session=<id>` for one session's events only.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/turns/t_91ee…/events?session=abc&store=st_9f2c…&after=0"
```

### GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/search

Text search over one session's stored history, newest first. Searched: the messages and input
items of its model requests (tool calls and tool results among them), each once, in the first call
that carried it; each call's kept reply; and the text of `turn.started` (the prompt), of a
program's `x.*` events, and of a `model.responded` whose reply is not kept (or is kept without its request). Not searched: system
blocks, instructions, tool definitions (codex's `additional_tools` items included). Case is ignored; `q` is found as written (no regex).
`q` is 1 to 256 bytes. Each hit has `source` (`request`, `reply` or `event`), `turn`, `call`,
`piece`, `seq`, `kind`, `role`, `block` (such as `tool_result`), a `snippet` of up to 80
characters each side, and `read`: the path that returns the whole of it. `limit` is 1 to 200
(default 20); send `before=<next_before>` for older hits until it is null. A page can hold fewer
than `limit` hits and still have a next page.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/sessions/abc/search?q=login&limit=5"
# {"store":"st_9f2c…","hits":[{"source":"request","turn":"t_5d0c…","call":"x-9f2c01ab-7","piece":12,"seq":1042,
#   "kind":"message","role":"user","block":"tool_result","snippet":"…func Login(…","read":"/api/v0/calls/x-9f2c01ab-7/pieces/12"}],"next_before":null}
```

### GET /api/v0/calls/{id}/context

Everything one model call's request carried, piece by piece, with sizes. `{id}` is the `exchange`
of the call's events. `full=false` leaves out each piece's `json`.

### GET /api/v0/calls/{id}/pieces/{n}

One piece of a call: `n` is its index in the context's `pieces`, from 0, or `reply` for the kept
reply. The body is the piece's bytes exactly as stored (`application/json`); `X-Piece-Kind`,
`X-Piece-Hash`, `X-Piece-Count` and `X-Piece-Label` describe it. 404 when there is no such piece.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$B/api/v0/calls/x-9f2c01ab-7/pieces/reply"
```

### POST /api/v0/events

A program writes its own event. `kind` is `x.<program>.<name>`; `session` is a known session or
`default`. Answers 201 with `seq` and `id`.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kind":"x.review.finding","session":"abc","text":"Line 12 reads past the end.","data":{"line":12}}' \
  $B/api/v0/events
```

### Agents: GET, POST /api/v0/agents, GET, PUT, DELETE /api/v0/agents/{id}

Saved agents: `{id, name, harness, access, model, key_env}`. `harness` is `claude` or `codex`;
`access` is `subscription` (the harness's own sign-in) or `openrouter` (a key read, when a turn
starts, from the environment variable `key_env` names, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` when absent; never the
key itself). An OpenRouter agent needs `model` in OpenRouter's naming, such as
`deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. `key_set` says whether the variable is set here. Main token only.
Before 0.2, `GET /api/v0/agents` was what `GET /api/v0/harnesses` is now.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $B/api/v0/agents
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"DeepSeek","harness":"codex","access":"openrouter","model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"}' \
  $B/api/v0/agents
# then start a turn with "agent":"<its id>"
```

### GET /api/v0/harnesses

Which harnesses this service can run an agent on: found on PATH, version, signed in, and for each
the access kinds and models a "+ Agent" form offers (`api` and `opencode` are listed, disabled).

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $B/api/v0/harnesses
```

### GET /api/v0/version

Which build of AgentBus this service is: what `agentbus version` prints. Main token only.

```sh
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $B/api/v0/version
# {"version":"0.1.0","commit":"5fea80b5…","modified":false}
```

### Jobs: POST /api/v0/jobs, GET /api/v0/jobs, POST /api/v0/jobs/{id}/review

A job is a requested turn, of kind `turn` or `review`, or an `apply` that
`POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/apply` makes. A runner takes it and runs it; its attempt
is its turn (the attempt id is the turn id, and `turn_started` says the turn started). A session's
first turn job names `agent` and `folder` (with `isolate: true` for a copy), or `repo` and `base` for a git worktree of its own; a
later one names `session` only, waits for the one before it, and keeps the session's model when it names none. Each job's `result` lists the files
it changed. A review job runs read-only in the reviewed job's workspace, in a session of its own,
and ends with `verdict` (`pass`, `fail` or `unknown`) and `findings`; any P1 makes it `fail`.
`POST /api/v0/jobs/{id}/cancel` stops one. `GET /api/v0/workspaces` lists the sessions'
workspaces, and `POST /api/v0/workspaces/{id}/close` closes one, which removes a worktree. All take
the main token. `/api/v0/runners` and `/api/v0/attempts/{id}/{start,heartbeat,events,finish}` are
the runner protocol: runners only.

```sh
curl -s $B/api/v0/jobs -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"kind":"turn","spec":{"agent":"claude","repo":"/path/to/repo","base":"main","prompt":"Add a test.","model":"haiku"}}'
# {"id":"job_…","kind":"turn","state":"queued","session":"6f1c…",…}
curl -s $B/api/v0/jobs/job_…/review -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"agent":"claude","model":"sonnet"}'
# {"id":"job_…","kind":"review","state":"queued","verdict":null,…}
```

### GET /api/v0/openapi.json

The OpenAPI 3.1 description, generated from the code at startup, with JSON Schemas for every body
and every event kind. No token.

```sh
curl -s $B/api/v0/openapi.json
```

## Events

Every event has `seq`, `id`, `kind`, `time`, `exchange` and `vendor`, and usually `session`. Other
fields depend on the kind. Ignore kinds and fields you do not know: v0 may add both.

The kind says who wrote the event; there is no separate source field. `model.*`, `tool.requested`,
`tool.completed`, `schema.unexpected` and `turn.completed` are observed by the gateway from the
agent's model traffic. `session.*`, `tool.refused`, `replay.failed`, `events.dropped` and the API's
own `turn.started` are written by AgentBus about its own actions. `x.<program>.<name>` is written
by a program and can never be a built-in kind. A job attempt's runner events (`workspace.*`,
`attempt.started`, `turn.created` and the like) are in `GET /api/v0/attempts/{id}/events`, not here.

| kind | what happened | main fields |
|---|---|---|
| `turn.started` | a person's message started a turn | `turn`, `text`, `agent`, `folder` (empty when the turn was not started through `POST /api/v0/turns`), `replay_from` (the earlier turn a replayed turn continues), `continuity` (`replay`, `resume` or `transcript`, on a next turn), `context` (with `transcript`: the earlier turns as text, put before `text` in the agent's prompt), `agent_id` (the saved agent that ran the turn), `recovered_from` and `recovered_reason` (the previous turn did not finish and how it ended; this turn continues after it) |
| `model.requested` | the harness sent a request to the model | `model`, `tools_offered`, `replayed` (history messages the gateway put in front) |
| `model.responded` | the model replied | `status`, `text`, `stop_reason`, `usage`, `cost_usd`, `cost_complete`, `error` |
| `tool.requested` | the model asked for a tool | `tool_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_input` |
| `tool.completed` | a tool's result reached the model | `tool_id`, `tool_output`, `tool_error` |
| `turn.completed` | the turn ended | `outcome` (`finished`, `partial`, `refused`, `unknown`), `stop_reason` |
| `session.opened` | a turn's agent started | `hold`, `agent`, `folder`, `turn` |
| `session.closed` | a turn's agent exited | `hold`, `exit_code`, `resume_id`, `turn`, `stopped` (the person stopped the turn), `unsettled` (its calls may not all be stored) |
| `session.registered` | older stores only; nothing writes it now | `agent`, `folder` |
| `events.dropped` | events were lost; those sessions' costs are incomplete | `dropped`, `sessions`, `all_sessions` |
| `schema.unexpected` | the vendor sent a shape the adapter does not know | `unexpected` (`where`, `value` or `field`) |
| `replay.failed` | a replayed turn's request could not be given the earlier turn's history; the gateway refused it and the turn fails | `error` |
| `tool.refused` | the gateway refused a tool call because its command matched a `forbid` entry; the agent did not run it | `tool_id`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `rule`, `text` (what the model is told) |
| `session.renamed` | the session was renamed with `PATCH /api/v0/sessions/{id}`; the latest names it | `title`, `old_title` (absent when it had none) |
| `x.<program>.<name>` | a program's own event | `text`, `data`, `turn`; `vendor` is `program` |

- `usage` is absent when the vendor sent none. Absent is not zero.
- Match a `tool.completed` to its `tool.requested` by `tool_id`, never by `turn`.
- A turn started through `POST /api/v0/turns` has the id the reply named on every event, however
  many model calls its agent makes. Traffic pointed at the gateway by hand gets a turn id hashed
  from the conversation.
- A turn's agent may end several model calls with `turn.completed`; its `state` in `GET /turns`
  comes from the agent's exit.
- `probe`: true on every event of a harness's own check, such as Claude Code's startup
  quota check. It has no turn. A cockpit may hide it.
